clue.text: Dog nips pants

parts.note: a boxer is a breed of dog
nips are small drinks of spirits, which in British pubs are called shorts

explanation.surface: A dog snapping at someone's trousers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nips' reads as a verb, the dog biting, but it is a plural noun: shots of spirits. In Britain 'pants' means underpants, not trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: In British usage pants are underwear, and loose cotton underwear for men is one such garment.

clue.text: Trust worker about live broadcast

indicators.note: about means the first word's letters go round the others

parts.note: a worker is a worker bee, a familiar crossword sense

indicators.note: broadcast means scattered widely, so these letters are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone trusts an employee covering a live broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'live broadcast' reads as a transmission, but 'broadcast' is the anagram signal, and 'worker' is the crossword's usual insect.
explanation.definitionFit: To trust someone is to have faith in what they say, a direct synonym as a verb.

clue.text: Cross Universal is screening an advertisement for a musical comedy

indicators.note: screening means hiding behind, so the outer letters shield the others inside them

parts.note: a cross is the letter X
U is the film-certificate abbreviation for universal
an ad is short for an advertisement

explanation.surface: An angry film studio shows an advert for a musical film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like 'angry' and 'Universal' like the studio, but they are X and U.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the title of a 1980 roller-disco film and later stage musical comedy.

clue.text: Extraordinarily rare opportunity to see a Hitchcock film

indicators.note: extraordinarily suggests something out of the ordinary, so these letters are put in an unusual order

parts.note: a window is an opportunity, as in a window of opportunity

explanation.surface: A rare chance to see a classic Hitchcock film.
explanation.definitionFit: This 1954 thriller starring James Stewart was directed by Alfred Hitchcock.

clue.text: Sales gimmick, praiseworthy, perhaps, to some extent

indicators.note: to some extent says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sales gimmick might be called praiseworthy, up to a point.
explanation.definitionFit: Hype is exaggerated publicity, a promotional trick used to drive sales.

clue.text: Rebuke for breaking into range

indicators.note: breaking into means forcing a way inside, so one word goes within the other

parts.note: reach means range, as in the reach of a weapon
pro means for, in favour of

explanation.surface: A telling-off for trespassing on the range.
explanation.definitionFit: To rebuke someone is to scold or express disapproval of them, a synonym.

clue.text: Less tense, one shirking work

definitions.meaning: comparative of slack, meaning looser or more relaxed
someone lazy who avoids doing their job

explanation.surface: A lazy worker is more relaxed than everyone else.
explanation.definitionFit: The comparative of slack means looser, and as a noun it names an idler who dodges duties.

clue.text: Father describing scented dish

indicators.note: describing here means drawing a line around, so the outer word encloses the other

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
olent is an old word meaning smelling or fragrant

explanation.surface: Dad talks about a fragrant dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'describing' looks like telling about, but it is used in the geometric sense of tracing round.
explanation.definitionFit: This Italian cornmeal porridge is served as a side or main course, so a dish.

clue.text: Salute attending members

parts.note: present means attending, being there
arms are limbs, and limbs are members of the body

explanation.surface: Members who attend a meeting give a salute.
explanation.definitionFit: This military command has soldiers hold rifles upright before the body as a mark of respect.

clue.text: Inspiring words from Guardiola, say

parts.note: Pep Guardiola is the Manchester City football manager
talk means say or speak

explanation.surface: A football manager delivers motivating words.
explanation.walkthrough: 'say' looks like 'for example' after Guardiola, but it is the verb. Pep Guardiola manages Manchester City, an English football club.
explanation.definitionFit: A short speech meant to encourage and motivate a team is a fitting phrase for inspiring words.

clue.text: Very large sum got from playing cards with children's author, mostly

parts.note: kings are playing cards

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter of the name is used

parts.note: Arthur Ransome wrote Swallows and Amazons

explanation.surface: Someone wins a fortune at cards against a children's writer.
explanation.walkthrough: Arthur Ransome is a British children's author, best known for Swallows and Amazons.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically, the price paid to free a captured monarch stands for an enormous amount of money.

clue.text: Call after what allows one to see County — call before game starts

indicators.note: after says the call piece follows the eyes and county pieces in the answer

parts.note: eyes are what let a person see
Down is a county of Northern Ireland
to look in is to call on someone, pay a short visit

explanation.surface: A shout made at a bingo hall just before the numbers begin.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is in Northern Ireland. The phrase is the bingo caller's traditional cry at the start of a game.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo callers announce this phrase to tell players to concentrate on their cards as play begins.

clue.text: See 10
Female seated in close cries

parts.note: she refers to a female

indicators.note: in means the second word is placed inside the first

parts.note: dear means close, as in a dear friend
sat means seated

explanation.surface: A woman sitting in a cathedral precinct weeps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close' looks like a cathedral close or 'near', but it is the adjective meaning intimate.
explanation.definitionFit: To weep a little is an idiom meaning becoming tearful, the same as crying.

clue.text: Start to enter man cave, wondrous place

indicators.note: start to means only the opening letter of the next word is taken

parts.note: a den is a private room, a man cave

explanation.surface: Getting into a man cave is a wonderful experience.
explanation.definitionFit: The biblical garden of paradise is a byword for a delightful place.

clue.text: Likely to happen, working with witty types to suppress article

indicators.note: to suppress means to hold down inside, so the article is held within the other letters

parts.note: on means working, functioning
a card is an amusing, witty person
the is the definite article

explanation.surface: Office comedians are told to cut out a newspaper article.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiomatically, something foreseen by fortune-telling cards is probable.

clue.text: Jazz pianist's skill starts to thrill audience that understands music

parts.note: art means skill, as in the art of conversation

indicators.note: starts to means the opening letters of the following words are taken

explanation.surface: A jazz pianist's talent thrills a knowledgeable audience.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'is', joining definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Art Tatum was a celebrated American jazz pianist known for his virtuosity.

clue.text: Golfer in row about golf clubs

indicators.note: about means the first word's letters go round the next

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
G is golf in the NATO phonetic alphabet
woods are a type of golf club, as opposed to irons

explanation.surface: A golfer in an argument about golf clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' looks like an argument but is a line, a tier; 'golf' is G from the phonetic alphabet, not part of 'golf clubs'.
explanation.definitionFit: Tiger Woods is one of the most successful professional golfers in history.

clue.text: Feeling of warmth around when opening in great Scottish city

indicators.note: around means the first word's letters surround the others

parts.note: a glow is a feeling of warmth
as means when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: opening in means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: A warm feeling when arriving in a great Scottish city.
explanation.definitionFit: Glasgow is the largest city in Scotland, on the River Clyde.

clue.text: Clue, perfect when shortened

indicators.note: when shortened means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: ideal means perfect

explanation.surface: A crossword clue that would be perfect if trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clue' looks like a crossword clue, but it means a notion, as in 'I haven't a clue'.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'not have a clue', a clue is a notion or inkling, a synonym.

clue.text: Good manners shown by Italian novelist entering house

indicators.note: entering means one word goes inside the other

parts.note: drum is British slang for a house or flat
Umberto Eco wrote The Name of the Rose

explanation.surface: An Italian writer shows good manners when entering a home.
explanation.walkthrough: Drum is old British slang for a house or dwelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Decorum is proper, polite behaviour, a synonym for good manners.

clue.text: Yacht station right in the middle of prime area

indicators.note: in the middle of means the letter goes into the centre of the word

parts.note: main means prime, chief

explanation.surface: A harbour for yachts right in the centre of a prime area.
explanation.definitionFit: A marina is a harbour where yachts and pleasure boats moor.

clue.text: Sudden turning point, tense in docudrama as so moving

indicators.note: moving means the letters are shifted into a new order

parts.note: T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A tense documentary drama so moving it changes a life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'moving' looks like 'touching' but tells you to rearrange T with DOCUDRAMA, AS and SO.
explanation.definitionFit: Saint Paul's conversion on his journey there gives the phrase for a sudden life-changing revelation.

clue.text: See 21
Religious song from that man on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means the word is heard spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: him refers to that man

explanation.surface: A religious song broadcast by a man on the radio.
explanation.definitionFit: A hymn is a song of praise sung in worship.

clue.text: Fairy lights, when lit, can make a fir ____!

definitions.text: Fairy lights, when lit, can make a fir ____!

indicators.note: lit means drunk, so these letters are tipsily rearranged; take a fir's letters out of the result

explanation.surface: Christmas lights on a fir tree make it pretty once switched on.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange FAIRY LIGHTS and remove the letters of A FIR: what is left is the missing word in the sentence.
explanation.definitionFit: Sightly means pleasing to look at, which is what lit decorations make a tree.

clue.text: English farm animals causing witty comment

parts.note: a pig and a ram are both farm animals, side by side

explanation.surface: English farm animals prompting a clever remark.
explanation.definitionFit: An epigram is a short, clever saying, a pithy witty remark.

clue.text: Old magazine alarms me now, curiously

indicators.note: curiously means strangely, so these letters are arranged in a strange order

explanation.surface: An old magazine now alarms the reader strangely.
explanation.definitionFit: A British women's weekly published from 1923 to 2018, now defunct, hence old.
